title: After the Fire
subtitle: The cloth market burned overnight; by dawn everyone has a culprit
coldOpen: 02:30. Fire sweeps forty shops in the cloth market.
06:00. Two posts name two different arsonists.
Traders stand in the ash asking who, and what now.

briefing.grievance: Forty traders lost their stock and their livelihood overnight. They want relief this week and the cause found honestly, not a scapegoat to make the anger stop.
knownFacts: Forty shops burned; nobody died; the fire started near a shared electrical panel.
The market had three fire-safety notices in two years, none acted on.
The insurance covers twelve of the forty shops.
unverifiedClaims: A post names a rival trader as the arsonist.
A second post says the owner burned it for insurance.
briefing.responsibility: You run the relief and the fire investigation. The traders need help, and the cause needs facts before names.
briefing.objective: Start relief now, secure the fire scene, and let the investigation name the cause before anyone names a person.

rightsMoments.question: A post names a trader as the arsonist and a crowd gathers at his shop. What does due process demand of the state?

options.text: Protect him, refuse to adopt the accusation without evidence, and act only on findings from the investigation.
options.feedback: Correct. The presumption of innocence binds the state; joining a mob’s accusation is itself a wrong.

options.text: Detain him to calm the crowd; the investigation can sort it out later.
options.feedback: Detaining a person to satisfy a crowd punishes him for an accusation, not for evidence.

options.text: Let the crowd and the trader settle it; the state should stay out.
options.feedback: The state has a duty to protect a person under threat and to prevent violence.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 21 protects life and liberty; the presumption of innocence means the state may not treat an accusation as a finding. It must protect the accused and follow evidence.
rightsMoments.why: The fire officer’s report pointed at a panel; naming a man would have turned an electrical fault into a lynching.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: A post names a trader as the arsonist and a crowd gathers at his shop. What must the state do?

options.a: Protect him and act only on real evidence.
options.b: Lock him up to calm the crowd.

feedback.a: Yes! Everyone is innocent until proven guilty.
feedback.b: No. Locking up an innocent man to calm a crowd is wrong.
feedback.c: The state must protect people in danger.

simple.principle: Everyone is innocent until proven guilty. The state must protect the accused and follow the evidence.
simple.why: The fire officer pointed at an electrical box. Naming a man would have turned a fault into a mob.
